sections.overview: The reed bunting is a passerine of genus Emberiza found across Britain and Ireland throughout the year.
sections.identification: Breeding males have a black head and white moustachial stripe; females are browner, and both sexes show white outer tail feathers.
sections.habitat: It breeds chiefly in reedbeds and other wetlands with dense emergent vegetation.
sections.diet: It eats insects during breeding and seeds in winter, also feeding invertebrates to its young.
sections.behavior: Northern populations migrate south in winter, and birds may join mixed flocks of finches and buntings.
sections.reproduction: The usual clutch contains four or five eggs, incubated by the female for about twelve to thirteen days.
sections.ecology: Its seasonal diet connects wetland breeding habitat with winter feeding in farmland.
sections.conservation: It is globally Least Concern but Amber-listed in the United Kingdom, where agricultural intensification reduced winter food availability.
